articles.title: SlothDesk AI: Let AI Handle the Busywork, Not Your Files
articles.excerpt: This is my submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 3: Slow and Steady. SlothDesk AI is a local-first productivity assistant that helps developers analyze documents, extract ac…
articles.body: This is my submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 3: Slow and Steady . What I Built SlothDesk AI is a local-first productivity assistant that helps developers analyze documents, extract action items, identify duplicate files, organize workspaces, and profile CSV datasets. Instead of letting an AI agent make uncontrolled filesystem changes, SlothDesk AI creates reviewable proposals and requires explicit approval before executing supported operations. Key features include: Document analysis for TXT, Markdown, CSV, and JSON files. AI-assisted summaries, tasks, decisions, and deadline extraction when local Gemma inference is available. SHA-256-based duplicate detection. Dry-run proposals, explicit approval, execution history, and rollback safeguards.
articles.author: Shaurya Tiwari

articles.title: I Ran Larastan at Every Level on Agent-Written Laravel Code: 4 Real Bugs, 3 Kinds of Noise
articles.excerpt: Originally published at hafiz.dev On October 12, Nuno Maduro posted that "it's kind of insane how much AI agents love nullables." His maths was simple. Every nullable doubles the number of states your…
articles.body: Originally published at hafiz.dev On October 12, Nuno Maduro posted that "it's kind of insane how much AI agents love nullables." His maths was simple. Every nullable doubles the number of states your code can be in, so a constructor with ten of them has over a thousand combinations to reason about. I wanted to see what that looks like in a real codebase, so I ran Larastan against one of mine at every level from 0 to 10. It's a production Laravel SaaS on Laravel 12 and Filament 4, about 25,000 lines across roughly 250 files in app/ , built over the last fifteen months. Most of that code was written by Claude Code, with me reviewing it. The four real bugs all showed up at level 0. Almost everything above that was typing noise with three causes, and two of them took one line each to fix.

articles.title: Legal Knowledge Bases on Premise: Compression, Tokens, and RAG Without Leaking Data
articles.excerpt: If you are an engineer asked to build "a searchable legal knowledge base" for a law firm or an in-house legal team, the easy part is the search UI. The hard part is everything underneath: hundreds of…
articles.body: If you are an engineer asked to build "a searchable legal knowledge base" for a law firm or an in-house legal team, the easy part is the search UI. The hard part is everything underneath: hundreds of gigabytes of scanned contracts, stamped pages, exhibit photos, and counterparty PDFs that nobody can open quickly, that blow past any context window if you try to feed them to a model, and that absolutely cannot leave the building. This piece is the hands-on, engineering-minded version of that problem — the one that talks about compression math, token budgets, and pipeline topology rather than vendor brochures.

articles.body: Introduction Artificial Intelligence is changing how we build modern applications. Traditionally, an application follows predefined business rules to process requests, retrieve data, and return responses. With AI-powered applications, we can go a step further by allowing a Large Language Model (LLM) to understand user intent and choose appropriate actions through controlled application tools. For example, imagine an e-commerce customer asking: "Can you tell me where my order is and when it will arrive?" articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.

articles.excerpt: 'Maybe Paradise isn’t always Paradise.'
articles.body: Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, " Lost on Paradise ", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week. Foster famously ghost-wrote the first " Star Wars " novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.
